payload.title: Exactly one Exocoetidae genome assembly is public, and it is unannotated
payload.statement: As retrieved on 2026-11-01, NCBI Datasets lists one assembly for the family Exocoetidae: Hirundichthys speculiger GCA_018398805.1, at scaffold level with no annotation. Ensembl lists no Exocoetidae species; medaka (Oryzias latipes) is the nearest Beloniformes in the Ensembl species list and can only be used as a labelled proxy. The assembly FASTA downloaded by this project has sha256 6f312a972a382295873cf1170771b0ef952f5f7772ce3b7bd19e3b49603c1052.
payload.context: A constraint on what comparative genomics is possible for a flying-fish project at all. Danio rerio and public sequence only. No observation of any Exocoetid fish was made by this project. Not claimed: that a flying fish can be built, that any zebrafish value transfers to an Exocoetid, or that any edit below has been performed.
assumptions: The NCBI Datasets and Ensembl listings read on 2026-11-01 are current.
Listing contents were read; assembly quality and completeness were not assessed.
limitations: A listing is not an assessment of assembly quality.
Not claimed: that no other Exocoetid assembly exists privately or unlisted.
The published genome paper (PMID 34306036) was retrieved at title level only; its abstract was not in the saved response.

payload.title: All 27 candidate fin-development proteins align somewhere in the Hirundichthys speculiger assembly, with controls passing, but two cannot be assigned to a paralog
payload.statement: miniprot 0.18-r281 (-t4 -N5 --outs=0.6, applied per assembly chunk) aligned 27 distinct Danio rerio candidate proteins to GCA_018398805.1 across three runs; every one has a best-aligning region. Best-hit amino-acid identity (PAF residue matches over alignment block length) ranges 0.447 (hoxd13a) to 0.989 (the actb1 positive control). Controls behaved: actb1 aligned at coverage 1.00 and identity 0.989, and three independently shuffled negative controls (fgf10a-, kcnh2a- and eda-shuffled, seed 12345) produced no hit at all. msxb, mapped in two runs on separately re-chunked copies of the assembly, returned the identical interval JAGFBZ010000863.1:508027-509355. Paralog controls added after review show that kcnh2a and kcnh2b best-hit the same region of JAGFBZ010001591.1 from the identical start coordinate 1301510 with the b query scoring HIGHER (identity 0.762 vs 0.610), so the detected region cannot be assigned to kcnh2a; tbx5b, fgf10b and kcnk5a resolve to scaffolds different from their a paralogs.
payload.context: Protein-to-genome alignment only. An alignment is not an annotation, an orthology assignment, a copy-number statement, or evidence that the locus is transcribed or does anything in Hirundichthys. Danio rerio and public sequence only. No observation of any Exocoetid fish was made by this project. Not claimed: that a flying fish can be built, that any zebrafish value transfers to an Exocoetid, or that any edit below has been performed.
assumptions: miniprot's PAF NM/blocklen is taken as the identity measure.

The assembly was split into five chunks of whole scaffolds to stay inside a 6 GB memory cap; because no scaffold was split, a best alignment lies wholly inside one chunk, which is why best hits are taken as chunk-independent while secondary-hit sets are not.
limitations: No orthology test was run (no reciprocal best hit, no synteny, no phylogeny), so no row names a paralog.
shha and shhb/twhh best-hit the same region of JAGFBZ010001012.1 (overlap 6364 bp) and cannot be assigned to distinct loci by this method.

The kcnh2a row must NOT be read as 'the kcnh2a ortholog is detectable': the kcnh2b query aligns to the same region at higher identity. kcnh2a is this project's primary candidate locus, so this is a limitation on the plan, not only on the table.

A span audit (scripts/audit_long_spans.py) shows the kcnh2a (278 kb), kcnh2b (239 kb) and cacna1g (298 kb) best hits each contain one intron-like gap of about 0.1 Mb and carry 2-4 frameshifts, with zero assembly-gap (N) content; whether these are large-intron genes or chaining artefacts was not determined. Treat them as 'something channel-like is present', not as located genes.
cacna1g best-hit coverage is 0.640, so its alignment is partial.
Alternative-hit counts per query are artefacts of applying -N5 and --outs=0.6 per chunk and must not be read as copy number.
No non-coding or regulatory sequence was examined.
The round-1 run was produced by a predecessor process and reviewed here, not re-run.

payload.title: Source statement: longfin(t2) is a cis-regulatory kcnh2a allele that lengthens fins by prolonging outgrowth
payload.statement: The abstract of PMID 34061172 (Development, 2021) states that the zebrafish mutant longfin(t2) overexpresses the ether-a-go-go-related K+ channel kcnh2a from chromosome 2; that disrupting kcnh2a in cis rescues the mutant, making longfin(t2) a regulatory kcnh2a allele; that the overgrowth comes from prolonged outgrowth periods rather than altered positional information or cell-level growth potency; that it acts tissue-autonomously within the intra-ray mesenchymal lineage; and that Kcnh2a appears to inhibit calcineurin output to supersede growth-cessation signals.
payload.context: The load-bearing source for treating fin size as a controllable outgrowth *duration* in a specific cell lineage, and for preferring a regulatory edit over a coding one. payload.title: Source statement: a kcnh2a x lat4a interaction in zebrafish phenocopies flying-fish fin proportions
payload.statement: The abstract of PMID 34534441 (Current Biology, 2021) states that a phylogenomic analysis of genome-wide variation in 35 species of flying fishes and relatives identified signatures in both coding and regulatory regions underlying convergent evolution of increased paired fin size and aerial gliding behaviours; that intersecting those signatures with distantly related zebrafish fin-size mutants implicated an L-type amino acid transporter, lat4a, and the potassium channel kcnh2a in fin proportion; and that the interaction between these loci in zebrafish closely phenocopies the observed fin proportions of flying fishes.
payload.context: The strongest published bridge this project found from zebrafish genetics to flying-fish morphology. Danio rerio and public sequence only. No observation of any Exocoetid fish was made by this project. Not claimed: that a flying fish can be built, that any zebrafish value transfers to an Exocoetid, or that any edit below has been performed.
assumptions: The abstract text as returned by Europe PMC is what the authors wrote.
limitations: Abstract-level read only; no figure, effect size, sample size or statistic was read.
'Closely phenocopies' is the authors' wording for fin proportion only; it says nothing about ray material properties, caudal asymmetry, launch muscle or gliding behaviour.
Which UniProt zebrafish entry the paper's 'lat4a' denotes is unresolved here (slc43a2a Q7ZUS0 is a 153 aa fragment; slc43a2b Q5PR35 is the 592 aa L-type amino acid transporter 4).
The 35-species variation data behind the analysis is not public to this project, so the convergence scan cannot be reproduced here.

payload.title: Source statement: retinoic acid scales the zebrafish pectoral fin bud through rcan2, Kcnk5b, Ca2+ and shha
payload.statement: The abstract of PMID 38527087 (PLoS Biology, 2024) states that intracellular K+ levels fall in a coordinated way during zebrafish pectoral fin bud growth; that overexpressing K+-leak channels coordinately increases bud proportions; that retinoic acid decreases K+ in bud tissues and up-regulates rcan2; that rcan2 overexpression increases bud growth and decreases K+ while CRISPR-Cas9 targeting of rcan2 does the reverse; that Rcan2-mediated growth depends on Kcnk5b; that Kcnk5b enhances depolarization via Na+ channels and this is required for its growth effect; and that Kcnk5b-induced shha transcription and bud growth require IP3R-mediated Ca2+ release and CaMKK activity.
payload.context: One of the few reads that places the K+/Ca2+ size-scaling mechanism in the *embryonic* fin bud rather than in adult regeneration, which matters because a wing must be built during development. payload.title: Source statement: cell-type-specific bioelectric manipulation separates fin size from fin-ray segment length
payload.statement: The abstract of the 2024 Development paper 'Cell-type-dependent bioelectric regulation of fin size and fin-ray segment length in zebrafish' states that expressing the hyperactive potassium channel mutant kcnk5b(W169L) or the dominant-negative connexin mutant Cx43(T154A) under cell-type-specific promoters had different effects by cell type: manipulation in keratinocytes primarily affected fin size, while manipulation in osteoblasts preferentially altered fin-ray segment length; that combining them produced enlarged fins with short segments or small fins with long segments; and that optogenetic manipulation showed membrane potential itself can regulate both.
payload.context: Establishes two separately addressable design knobs — overall appendage size and skeletal element length — which is what a wing design needs, since a long fin with wrong ray segmentation is not a wing. payload.title: A gene tree with a passing positive control places the one kcnh2-like region of the Hirundichthys speculiger assembly with kcnh2b, not kcnh2a
payload.statement: A maximum-likelihood protein gene tree (MAFFT v7.505 then IQ-TREE 2.0.7, LG+G4, 1000 ultrafast bootstrap and 1000 SH-aLRT replicates, seed 12345, Nebius job aijob-e00knz7gwwqck9nksp, state COMPLETED) places the four miniprot-predicted proteins from JAGFBZ010001591.1 in a clade (support 99.8/100) sister to zebrafish kcnh2b (99/100), with kcnh2a outside that pair (99.2/100). Its positive control passes: the four predictions from JAGFBZ010001790.1, which an earlier reciprocal test called kcnh6a-like, form a clade with zebrafish kcnh6a and nothing else (94.4/97). Therefore the one kcnh2-like region detectable in this assembly is kcnh2b-like, and this project has located no kcnh2a-like region in it. The three earlier readings of the same question did not agree, and the tree is taken as the answer because it is the only one of them with an outgroup and a positive control. (1) Forward mapping: the kcnh2a and kcnh2b queries best-hit the same region of JAGFBZ010001591.1 from the identical start coordinate 1301510, with kcnh2b at higher identity (0.762 vs 0.610). (2) Reciprocal test: miniprot --trans predicted 8 distinct proteins from that scaffold and each was aligned against all 10 zebrafish kcnh family members (Biopython PairwiseAligner, global, BLOSUM62); 5 rank kcnh2b first and 3 rank kcnh2a first, and for the longest and most complete prediction (1325 aa) kcnh2a wins on alignment score by 631 while kcnh2b wins on percent identity over aligned columns (0.827 vs 0.674). The verdict therefore depends on a scoring choice. (3) The obvious alternative region, kcnh2a's second-best forward hit on JAGFBZ010001790.1, is accounted for: all 10 predicted proteins there rank kcnh6a first with margins 325-1544. By contrast the same reciprocal test resolves the shha/shhb collision cleanly, with 5 of 5 predicted proteins from JAGFBZ010001012.1 ranking shha first.
payload.context: kcnh2a is this project's primary candidate locus for fin-size engineering (the longfin gene), so this means the proposed edit has no located target in the only public Exocoetidae assembly: the best candidate region has been positively assigned to the other paralog. Danio rerio and public sequence only. No observation of any Exocoetid fish was made by this project. Not claimed: that a flying fish can be built, that any zebrafish value transfers to an Exocoetid, or that any edit below has been performed.
assumptions: ASSUMED: that a miniprot protein prediction from an unannotated assembly is a usable proxy for the protein the region encodes.
ASSUMED: that the 10 UniProt entries used represent the zebrafish kcnh family adequately; kcnh8a and kcnh8b were not retrievable and are missing.
limitations: Absence of a located kcnh2a-like region is NOT evidence that Hirundichthys speculiger lacks the gene. The assembly is scaffold-level and unannotated; a divergent or fragmented ortholog would look the same.
A gene tree places sequences by substitution likelihood; it does not establish orthology without synteny, which was not run.
The four predictions come from one genomic region, so they are not independent sequences and their own clade is partly an artefact of that.

The zebrafish kcnh2a entry is 1253 aa and kcnh2b's is 837 aa; the tree does not control for the length difference, and that difference is the likely mechanical cause of the earlier score-vs-identity disagreement.
The inputs are miniprot predictions from an unannotated assembly, not sequenced transcripts.
kcnh8a and kcnh8b were not retrievable from UniProt, so the zebrafish family in the tree is 10 of its members, not all of them.
One run, one operator, not independently reviewed.

payload.title: No kcnh2a-like locus is detectable in the one public Exocoetidae assembly, while 9 of 10 other KCNH paralogs are
payload.statement: A low-stringency whole-assembly search with the zebrafish kcnh2a protein alone (miniprot 0.18-r281, -N 20 --outs=0.3 --outc=0.05) finds no region beyond the 7 already known. A gene tree of the 5 previously untested ones (Nebius job aijob-e00k03g7vbmk6smbkh, COMPLETED) places each with a different paralog: kcnh6b, kcnh7 twice, kcnh4a and kcnh5a, with both carried-forward controls reproducing at 99.3/100 and 99.6/100. A family-wide census then mapped all 10 zebrafish KCNH queries over the whole assembly, merged 65 hit intervals into 14 distinct KCNH-like loci and placed them on one tree (job aijob-e00nvq278rsze2f6bp, COMPLETED): 9 of the 10 zebrafish paralogs receive at least one flying-fish locus and the single exception is kcnh2a. The KCNH family is therefore well represented in this assembly while the kcnh2a gap is specific.
payload.context: kcnh2a is the longfin gene and one of the two loci a flying-fish phylogenomic study names for paired-fin size, so it is this project's primary candidate locus. The consequence is that an edit aimed at the Exocoetid kcnh2a has no located target in the only public assembly for the family. Danio rerio and public sequence only. No observation of any Exocoetid fish was made by this project. Not claimed: that a flying fish can be built, that any zebrafish value transfers to an Exocoetid, or that any edit below has been performed.
assumptions: ASSUMED: that a miniprot prediction from an unannotated assembly is a usable proxy for the protein a region encodes.
ASSUMED: that 10 UniProt entries adequately represent the zebrafish KCNH family; kcnh8a and kcnh8b were not retrievable, so some of the 14 loci may belong to paralogs absent from the reference set.
limitations: This is a statement about GCA_018398805.1, NOT about Hirundichthys speculiger and NOT about Exocoetidae. The assembly is an explicitly draft, scaffold-level, unannotated genome, and a missing or fragmented single gene is the expected failure mode of such an assembly.
A sufficiently divergent Exocoetid kcnh2a could be placed with a neighbouring paralog rather than appearing as a kcnh2a sister, which would produce this same result.

Three of the 14 locus assignments are weakly supported and should be read as unresolved (42.7/68, 23.4/62, and one with no recovered support value); none of the three was assigned to kcnh2a, so dropping them does not change the result.
A gene tree places sequences by substitution likelihood; no synteny was used in the census.
The published flying-fish phylogenomics that names kcnh2a (PMID 34534441) used 35 species with its own sequencing, not this assembly, so nothing here contradicts it.
One operator, not independently reviewed; a model-sensitivity re-run was submitted separately.

payload.title: The candidate regulatory windows carry above-composition motif structure in aggregate, in both species, and no per-window claim survives
payload.statement: Three Nebius passes scanned 879 JASPAR2024 CORE vertebrate motifs against claude-evo's 19 held-out 2 kb windows and composition-matched shuffles of them, holding the motif set constant by digest across all three. Pass 1 (pooled GC-matched thresholds, 2 shuffles per window) gave zebrafish +7.0 [-11.0, +25.0] and flying fish +55.7 [+29.6, +81.8]. Pass 2 (per-window thresholds from each window's own 20 doublet-verified shuffles) gave zebrafish +51.7 [37.3, 66.2] and flying fish +57.4 [39.1, 75.7], 19/19 windows positive, withdrawing pass 1's species asymmetry as an artefact of the pooled threshold. Pass 3 (the same 20 shuffles split 10 to calibrate and 10 as the null) gave zebrafish +27.1 [7.9, 46.3] and flying fish +26.8 [12.0, 41.6]. What survives all three designs is an aggregate excess of motif matches over composition-matched shuffles in both species. What does not survive is the effect size and every per-window claim: mean |z| falls to 1.39 and 1.57 under the held-out design, with only 2 of 10 and 4 of 9 windows above z = 2.
payload.context: The Evo 2 harness named this scan as the follow-up neither harness had run. It ran its own version independently with a different thresholding rule and reports the same direction (+125.3 excess hits, CI [61.0, 189.7]), so two independently written implementations agree on the direction. Danio rerio and public sequence only. No observation of any Exocoetid fish was made by this project. Not claimed: that a flying fish can be built, that any zebrafish value transfers to an Exocoetid, or that any edit below has been performed.
assumptions: ASSUMED: that JASPAR vertebrate PFMs are applicable to teleost sequence; no fish-specific motif set was used.

The windows are claude-evo's computed objects, reused verbatim and hash-verified: zebrafish ones TSS-anchored on GRCz11, flying-fish ones anchored upstream of a PREDICTED start codon in an unannotated assembly.
limitations: A motif match is a sequence-pattern match. It is NOT a bound transcription factor, NOT an enhancer, and NOT evidence of expression or function.
No per-window, per-gene or per-motif statement is supportable, so these windows cannot be ranked against each other by this result.
Cross-species comparison of effect MAGNITUDE is composition-confounded and is not made; only the within-species aggregates are reported.

Two of the nine flying-fish windows sit at loci this project's own cross-check assigns to a different paralog than their label (kcnk5b and fgf10a), so their gene labels are in doubt independently of this result.
Pass 1's reported species asymmetry is withdrawn. It is retained in the record only to show what the design change did.

payload.title: Hypothesis: the flying-fish pectoral wing is reachable by extending outgrowth duration in ray mesenchyme alone
payload.statement: HYPOTHESIS, with no evidence of any kind offered for it here. If the Exocoetid pectoral fin is enlarged by the same mechanism that enlarges the longfin(t2) zebrafish fin, then the minimal edit that increases fin length is one that extends the outgrowth period in the intra-ray mesenchymal lineage and nowhere else, rather than one that increases growth rate, cell number or positional values. The prediction that makes it falsifiable: an edit restricted to that lineage should change fin length without changing ray segment count per unit length, and an edit restricted to osteoblasts should do the opposite.
payload.context: Written down so it can be attacked. It is the design assumption behind perturbation rows P1 and P4 in PLAN.md. Danio rerio and public sequence only. No observation of any Exocoetid fish was made by this project. Not claimed: that a flying fish can be built, that any zebrafish value transfers to an Exocoetid, or that any edit below has been performed.
assumptions: ASSUMED, not shown: that the Exocoetid wing and the zebrafish longfin phenotype share a mechanism. Nothing read or run here tests this.
ASSUMED, not shown: that fin proportion is the binding constraint on gliding, rather than ray stiffness or muscle power.
limitations: This is a hypothesis. It is not evidence, it has not been tested, and no experiment in PLAN.md has been performed.
No Exocoetid expression, timing or cell-lineage data exists in this project.
Even if true, it addresses trait T1 only and leaves T3, T5, T6 and T8 (caudal asymmetry, ray material, launch muscle, behaviour) entirely unaddressed.

payload.title: Two candidate edits for flying-fish traits destroy other required traits in the same organism
payload.statement: Reading the abstracts together exposes two conflicts that any flying-fish design has to resolve. First: triple hoxa13a/hoxa13b/hoxd13a mutant rays become shorter and thicker and lose joints, bifurcations and actinotrichia, resembling acanthomorph spiny rays (PMID 41739864) — so the edit that moves rays toward a stiffer, spine-like character also shrinks the fin and deletes the collagen fibres, opposing the enlarged-wing trait. Second: eda knockout zebrafish lack scales, fin rays, pharyngeal teeth and gill rakers (PMID 41344457) — so a scale or keel edit through eda is not separable from the fin-ray programme. Neither conflict was resolvable from what was read.
payload.context: A derived reading of two source abstracts, not a new experiment. Its value is that it rules out two otherwise attractive edit routes before any bench cost is incurred. Danio rerio and public sequence only. No observation of any Exocoetid fish was made by this project. Not claimed: that a flying fish can be built, that any zebrafish value transfers to an Exocoetid, or that any edit below has been performed.
assumptions: The two abstracts' phenotype descriptions are taken at face value.
ASSUMED: that these zebrafish pleiotropies would also hold in an Exocoetid. Untested.
limitations: Abstract-level reads on both sides; no dosage series, conditional or cell-type-restricted version of either edit was examined, and either could dissolve the conflict.
Danio rerio only.
This is a conflict between published phenotypes, not a demonstration that no design can satisfy both.

payload.title: Which zebrafish UniProt entry is the 'lat4a' of the flying-fish convergence papers?
payload.known_state: Two independent papers name lat4a as a fin-size locus with a convergent signature in flying fishes (PMID 34534441) and a convergent amino-acid change shared with syngnathids, reported as confirmed in vitro (PMID 40689752). UniProt's zebrafish entries are slc43a2a (Q7ZUS0, 153 aa, a fragment) and slc43a2b (Q5PR35, 592 aa, annotated 'L-type amino acid transporter 4'). This project mapped both to GCA_018398805.1 and they best-hit different scaffolds (JAGFBZ010001224.1 and JAGFBZ010000485.1), so two distinct LAT4-like regions are detectable.
payload.question: Which gene — and therefore which Exocoetid scaffold region — do the two papers mean by lat4a, and which codon carries the reported convergent change?
payload.novelty_status: Not a field open problem; it is a gap in this project's reading. Resolvable by one full-text read.
payload.data_access: Both papers are indexed in Europe PMC; PMID 34534441 is Current Biology (access not checked), PMID 40689752 is Integrative Zoology (access not checked). The assembly and both alignments are already on disk in this repository.
acceptance_criteria: A full-text read of PMID 34534441 and PMID 40689752 names the gene identifier or accession used, and the residue position of the convergent change.
The named identifier is matched to one of the two mapped scaffold regions, with the amino-acid position located in that alignment.
falsifiers: The papers use a gene identifier that corresponds to neither slc43a2a nor slc43a2b, in which case the candidate locus in this project is wrong.
The convergent change is reported only in Exocoetid species other than H. speculiger and is absent from the H. speculiger assembly.
payload.next_action: Read the two full texts for the gene identifier and residue position, then extract the corresponding codon from the aligned region of GCA_018398805.1 recorded in data/round2/mapping_summary_round2.json.
required_capabilities: sequence extraction from a local FASTA
payload.cost_stop_bounds: Two full-text reads and one short sequence-extraction script; under an hour. Stop if neither paper states a usable identifier, and record that as the finding.
downstream_uses: Unblocks analysis G4 in PLAN.md section 3.
Unblocks perturbation row P2 (single-codon knock-in), which cannot be designed against an unknown paralog.

payload.title: No candidate gene is known to this project for the hypocercal caudal fin of flying fishes
payload.known_state: Exocoetid caudal fins have an enlarged lower lobe used at the water surface. Zebrafish caudal fin symmetry is patterned by a central and two peripheral organizers (PMID 35403297, abstract level) and caudal fin shape imprinted in late embryogenesis is re-patterned by Shh signalling (PMID 40853969, title level). A targeted Europe PMC query for Exocoetid or Beloniform caudal and hypural asymmetry returned 34 hits, none of which was an Exocoetid caudal morphology or genetics paper with an abstract in the response.
payload.question: What genetic or developmental difference makes the Exocoetid caudal fin hypocercal, and is any of it shared with the zebrafish caudal symmetry organizers?
payload.novelty_status: Whether the field has addressed this was not established; the queries run here found nothing, which is weak evidence of absence.
payload.data_access: No Exocoetid caudal morphometry, expression or sequence data specific to the trait was found. The only Exocoetid assembly is unannotated and there is no Exocoetid transcriptome in anything retrieved.
downstream_uses: Marks perturbation row P11 in PLAN.md as having no designable edit, which prevents an invented one.

payload.title: Nothing retrieved establishes Exocoetid husbandry, spawning, embryo access or transgenesis
payload.known_state: Every engineering method in PLAN.md section 5 that is rated feasible is feasible *in zebrafish*. Across 45 Europe PMC queries, no record retrieved described captive Exocoetid breeding, embryo collection, microinjection or transgenesis. Cytogenetic work on three species used chromosome preparations, not living embryos (PMID 42325591).
payload.question: Can Exocoetid embryos be obtained and injected at all, and by whom, or is every 'edit a flying fish' route closed at the husbandry step regardless of the genetics?
payload.novelty_status: This is a gap in this project's knowledge, not a claim that the field has never done it.
payload.data_access: No source read addresses it. Marine station and fisheries literature was not searched.
downstream_uses: Bounds the whole project: it separates 'a zebrafish with flying-fish fin proportions', which is scoped, from 'a flying fish', which is not.

source.access: Files in this repository at the branch named in the locator. The computation was run by this project; nobody has re-run it, so it is not independent evidence.
